broadcast.title: Terminal broadcast
broadcast.commandPlaceholder: Enter a command. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line.
broadcast.liveConfirmDescription: Every key, control sequence, and paste from this terminal will be sent to the selected terminals. They may be in different interactive states. Password-prompt detection is incomplete, so verify every target before entering secrets. Ctrl+Shift+B stops broadcasting.

broadcast.multilinePasteDescription_other: This paste contains multiple lines and will be sent to {{count}} terminals.

broadcast.stoppedForPromptDescription: A password prompt was detected. Sensitive input will remain in the source terminal.

settings.monitorDesc: Tune how often SSH server metrics refresh while the monitor is visible.

settings.sftpDesc: Configure file manager behavior for remote directories.
settings.sftpPasteUploadDesc: When enabled, Ctrl+V or Cmd+V in the SFTP panel uploads copied local files and folders. Clipboard text is ignored.

settings.devtoolsDesc: Open the developer tools window for debugging.
settings.tabWidthDesc: Control the width of title-bar and split-group tabs.
settings.tabWidthModeDesc: Adaptive width follows each title. Standard width gives every tab the same width.

secretStorage.title: Secret Storage
secretStorage.description: Choose where SSH passwords are persisted. Hybrid mode (recommended) stores all passwords in an encrypted vault and saves the master password in the system keyring for automatic unlock.
secretStorage.enableVaultDesc: Required for Auto fallback and App vault mode.
secretStorage.lockVaultHybridDesc: After locking, you'll need to enter the vault password manually next time (auto-unlock will be paused).
secretStorage.promptUnlockOnStartup: Prompt to unlock vault on startup
secretStorage.promptUnlockOnStartupDesc: Show an unlock dialog when tTerm starts. The vault password is never saved.
secretStorage.startupUnlockDesc: Enter your vault password to use saved SSH passwords in this session. tTerm does not store this password.
secretStorage.startupPromptEnabledDesc: tTerm will ask you to unlock the app vault on startup.
secretStorage.startupPromptDisabledDesc: tTerm will not show the vault unlock prompt on startup.
secretStorage.keyringUnavailableDesc: Passwords can only be persisted after you unlock the app vault.
secretStorage.copyDesc: Copy saved SSH and jump-host passwords between the system keyring and the app vault. Existing target entries are overwritten.
secretStorage.copyCompleteDesc: Copied {{copied}} item(s). Skipped {{skipped}} item(s) with no source password.
secretStorage.savedPasswordsDesc: Review SSH and jump-host passwords linked to current profiles.
secretStorage.noSavedPasswords: No saved passwords are available from the active backend.
secretStorage.deleteSavedSecretConfirm: Delete the saved password for {{label}}? This removes the matching system keyring and vault entries.

modeDescriptions.auto: Use the system keyring when available, then fall back to the unlocked app vault.
modeDescriptions.system: Use only the operating system credential store.
modeDescriptions.vault: Use only the app vault. Unlock it before saving or loading passwords.
modeDescriptions.hybrid: All passwords are stored in the encrypted app vault. The vault master password is saved in the system keyring so the vault unlocks automatically on startup.
modeDescriptions.memory: Do not persist passwords; keep them only for the current app session.

secretStorage.hybridSetup: Set a vault password to enable hybrid mode. It will be saved in your system keyring for automatic unlock.
secretStorage.changeVaultPasswordDesc: Update the vault master password. All stored secrets will be re-encrypted with the new password.
secretStorage.passwordChangedDesc: The vault password has been updated. Your system keyring entry was also refreshed.
